extra.message: User input from the 'id' query parameter is concatenated directly into the SQL query string passed to cursor.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. '1 OR 1=1') to dump the users table including session tokens.
The 'password' parameter (and username, only weakly filtered by a \w regex) is concatenated into the login SQL query. Supplying password="' OR '1'='1" bypasses authentication entirely.
The 'msg' query parameter is returned unescaped and interpolated into the HTML template via str.format in TemplateHandler.get_content, allowing reflected cross-site scripting.
Guestbook comments stored via the 'comment' parameter (line 88) are rendered into HTML table cells without any escaping, allowing persistent/stored XSS for every visitor of /guestbook.

The user-controlled 'domain' parameter is joined into a shell command string executed with subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True). Payloads like 'www.google.com;ifconfig' achieve arbitrary OS command execution.

do_BDR passes the raw request path (self.path[1:]) directly to subprocess.check_output with shell=True. Any client sending a BDR HTTP request with a crafted path (e.g. 'BDR /id HTTP/1.1' when risk>=3) achieves remote command execution.

Attacker-supplied base64 data from the 'object' parameter is deserialized with pickle.loads(). Pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution (the class itself ships an RCE __reduce__ payload as proof).
The 'path' query parameter is passed to open(os.path.abspath(path), 'rb') without any directory restriction, allowing arbitrary local file read via absolute paths or '../' traversal.

StaticHandler.find opens './{}'.format(path) using the raw request path with no normalization or directory validation. A request for /../db/users.xml (or encoded variants) reads arbitrary files outside the static directory.

When the 'path' parameter contains '://', it is passed to urllib.request.urlopen(), letting an attacker make the server fetch arbitrary URLs (http://, file://, etc.), enabling server-side request forgery.

The user-controlled 'path' parameter is interpolated unescaped into a JavaScript window.location.replace() call, enabling open redirects to attacker-controlled sites and JavaScript string-breakout XSS.
SessionFixation.run interpolates the user-controlled 'path' parameter into window.location without validation, allowing open redirect and script-context injection.
The SESSIONID cookie is set directly from the attacker-controlled 'session' query parameter, allowing an attacker to fix a victim's session identifier and later hijack the authenticated session.
Session tokens are generated with random.sample() from the non-cryptographic random module instead of the secrets module, making session IDs predictable and vulnerable to session hijacking.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: ExecutionAfterRedirect performs its 'authorization' check only via a client-side JavaScript redirect; the privileged admin content is rendered and sent in the HTTP response regardless of authentication state (execution after redirect).

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The /settings handler updates the user's email address based solely on a GET parameter with no CSRF token, no Origin/Referer check, and state change via GET — an attacker can change a victim's account settings cross-site.

The /danger endpoint deletes the user's account via a simple GET parameter and the server (handlers.py) sends no X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors directive, allowing clickjacking of this irreversible destructive action.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers

extra.message: The SQL query selects the 'session' column and the result is rendered verbatim into the HTML table (lines 44-62), exposing live session tokens of all users to anyone who can reach /sqli, enabling session hijacking.

Raw exception text (str(ex)) is sent to the client via send_error (see also attacks.py:40-41 returning sqlite3 errors to the browser), leaking internal error details useful for exploiting SQL injection and other attacks.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Hardcoded backdoor credentials: username 'dsvpwa' with password 'dsvpwa' always authenticate successfully regardless of the user database.

User passwords (admin, guest, loella, weitzel) are stored in plaintext in db/users.xml and loaded unhashed into the SQLite users table by dsvpwa/server.py:44-46; credentials are recoverable by anyone with file or database read access.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: Session cookies are set via morsel.OutputString() without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes, leaving SESSIONID accessible to JavaScript (amplifying the many XSS flaws) and sent over cleartext HTTP.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The server explicitly disables the browser XSS filter (X-XSS-Protection: 0) and sets a wildcard Content-Security-Policy (default-src * 'unsafe-inline') that permits inline scripts from any origin, while sending no X-Frame-Options — compounding XSS and clickjacking exposure.

The TLS context explicitly re-enables SSLv3 (clears OP_NO_SSLv3), enables TLS compression (clears OP_NO_COMPRESSION, enabling CRIME), and disables server cipher preference, weakening transport security to obsolete, vulnerable protocol versions.

cwe: CWE-757: Selection of Less-Secure Algorithm During Negotiation
